rows.title: Realtime safety on the audio thread
rows.gaps: rtsafety_probe counts allocations in process() while it sweeps parameter ids 1-99 only, and runs no planted fault of its own. No RealtimeSanitizer job (needs upstream clang on Linux CI, Wave B). No lint of the realtime ban list.

rows.title: Thread races between UI, host and audio threads
rows.gaps: CI's sanitize job runs ThreadSanitizer over the compiled oracles, which are single-threaded by construction. No stress harness that hammers parameters, presets and save/load during render (Wave B).

rows.title: NaN, Inf and denormals
rows.gaps: The legacy output guard now latches and counts (nan_latch_check; hostile_events_check reads the real plugin's counter), but the count reaches no user-visible surface yet. horde 2's engine has no output guard: it ends in tanh, and a NaN passes through. Flush-to-zero is set nowhere (audited 2026-10-08); denormals are snapped in software in the swarm and sub cores, and no per-block FTZ is planned without an ADR.
rows.tripwire: NaN events: 0, plus the guard's trip count

rows.title: Sample-rate and block-size dependence
rows.gaps: Rate and block-size checks exist per mechanism. No full matrix rendering each reference patch at 44.1/48/96/192 kHz and blocks of 1, 7, 64, 512 and varying, compared on perceptual features.

rows.title: Long-run drift
rows.gaps: stability_check holds RMS drift, f0 drift, peak and non-finite count over 60 simulated seconds of the legacy SAW core in verify full (the ten-minute run is by hand). No 4-hour nightly soak per engine with level, DC and spectral-centroid bounds.

rows.title: Numerical stability at the edges
rows.gaps: Note-stream fuzzing, hostile-event checks and a high-coupling lifecycle probe exist. No property-based fuzz of the full parameter space with automation sweeps, modulation stacking and output-bound assertions.

rows.title: State and preset compatibility
rows.gaps: Three state fixtures load bit-identically and parameter ids are reserved. No per-release saved-state corpus rendered in CI and no append-only parameter-id check (Wave C).

rows.title: Host integration edge cases
rows.gaps: pluginval runs at strictness 10 in CI (Windows on every PR, macOS on main pushes). auval is a manual step, not a gate. No clap-validator, scripted host matrix, or two-instance shared-state test.
rows.tripwire: Validators: all green, N hosts tested

rows.title: Perceptual quality not heard on monitors
rows.gaps: A fitted aliasing metric across the keyboard. No per-patch suite for true peak, DC, sub-20 Hz energy or mono-sum loss with stored thresholds.
rows.tripwire: A spectrum report per engine, red flags only

rows.title: The parity-golden trap
rows.gaps: Parity with the prototypes is provisional under ADR-187. Few closed-form, conservation or metamorphic tests independent of the prototypes, and no count of goldens carrying an independent check.
rows.tripwire: Goldens with independent check: N of M

rows.title: Build and platform divergence
rows.gaps: horde 2 builds are pinned contraction-off with an FMA control, and signing is in the release pipeline. x86_64 is exercised only by CI's Linux sanitizer job and the Windows build and validation; no parity run on x86_64 at the shipped Release flags, and no audit of the full flag set.

rows.title: Worst-case CPU and licensing exposure
rows.gaps: The B439 budget and the CPU ledger exist as documents, and the CPU measurement is run by hand; no per-release gate on the worst-case patch. Releases carry a generated SBOM, but there is no license allow-list audit (Wave C).
rows.tripwire: Worst-case CPU: X% of budget; Licenses: clear

rows.title: Symptom clamping
rows.gaps: No check flags a new clamp, isfinite guard or limiter in DSP code that lacks a root-cause trace. Review only.
rows.tripwire: New DSP clamps without a root-cause trace: 0

rows.title: Snapshot of the bug
rows.gaps: No check that a new golden names its independent justification (closed form, prototype plus listening sign-off, or measurement).
rows.tripwire: New goldens without a named justification: 0

rows.title: Tolerance creep
rows.gaps: tolerance_registry_check pins 138 tolerances (ACCEPTANCE.md and the C++ checks) and fails on any unapproved change or unregistered newcomer. Not yet: the JS labs and oracles (.mjs), integer thresholds written inline, tolerances computed from other names; 75 entries have no governing ADR yet; it cannot prove an `approved` reference came from the human.

rows.title: Quiet disabling
rows.gaps: test_table_check makes every check declare whether ./verify runs it, and cross-checks the claim. weakening_check counts skips, suppressions, disabled sanitizers, soft-fails, UNWIRED declarations and DSP guards against a baseline and fails on any increase. Not yet: markers assembled by macro, and proof that an `approved` reference was written by the human rather than an agent.
rows.tripwire: Skips, suppressions and disabled sanitizers: no increase

rows.title: Happy-path tests
rows.gaps: No check that each engine test suite includes extreme-parameter and automation-sweep cases.
rows.tripwire: Engine suites without extreme and sweep cases: 0

rows.title: Confident wrong explanations
rows.gaps: No diff-only reviewer agent yet checks that a PR's stated cause is what the diff changes.
rows.tripwire: PRs whose stated cause the diff does not change: 0

rows.title: Cross-agent contradiction
rows.gaps: No seam-registry gate on shared-state and threading changes before merge.
rows.tripwire: Shared-state changes outside the seam registry: 0
